trial_court: Metropolitan Magistrate, Traffic Court - II, Bengaluru (Crl.Misc.No.147/2014)
case_name: Smt. Anitha.G vs Sri. Raghu. R
acts_cited_auto: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

acts_cited.act: Protection of Women from DV Act, 2005

facts_of_case: Petitioner and respondent were married in 2013. Petitioner claims domestic violence and seeks relief under Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005.

legal_principles.principle: A person's concealment of material facts can be a ground for divorce.
legal_principles.held: The respondent has caused domestic violence by demanding for dowry and also ill-treated her and has subjected her to severe acts of domestic violence by way of innumerable physical and mental torture.

legal_principles.principle: A person's concealment of incurable mental illness can be a ground for divorce.
legal_principles.held: The respondent then took the petitioner to the Doctor who treated the petitioner before marriage at BGS hospital at Kengeri. The Doctor disclosed that the petitioner was suffering from epilepsy and the doctor informed the respondent and his parents that, the petitioner is to be on medication continuously and she might not be able to bear children.
use_in: cases involving concealment of medical conditions

outcome.final_order: The court granted the petitioner's petition for protection order under Section 18 of the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005.

keywords: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
